page: Amazon Web Services c7gn.12xlarge is a compute-optimized instance hosted on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and driven by 48 dedicated ARM64 Neoverse-V1 cores running at 2.6 GHz. The architecture uses a single thread per physical core, providing 48 dedicated hardware execution threads. The system includes 96.0 GB of memory, establishing a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The cache structure provides 64 KB L1 data and 1.0 MB L2 cache per core, backed by a 32 MB shared L3 cache. Cryptographic processing is accelerated via hardware-level AES instructions, though x86-specific vector extensions are not supported on this ARMv8 profile.

Hardware bundling on the c7gn.12xlarge prioritizes networking over local attachments. The instance includes no onboard NVMe storage and contains zero GPUs, requiring remote EBS volumes for non-volatile data persistence. However, network throughput is exceptionally high, with a baseline network bandwidth allocation of 150 Gbps managed by dedicated Nitro hardware.

Benchmark data reflects strong multi-core scalability and high memory throughput alongside moderate single-threaded performance. The instance reached 73,464.53 on stress-ng multi-core testing, 19,531.0 on Geekbench multi-core, and achieved a top-tier PassMark memory score of 3,164.0. In application-focused metrics, it sustained 64.06 GB/sec in static web serving throughput, 31,262.01 in PassMark database operations, and 76.81 million operations per second in Redis SET tests. Conversely, single-core metrics fall into the average range, including a Geekbench single-core score of 1,540.0 and LLM prompt processing rates between 8.44 and 1,768.52 tokens per second.

With its 150 Gbps network capacity and dense dedicated core allocation, the c7gn.12xlarge offers favorable efficiency for network-constrained workloads and highly parallel operations. It is well suited for high-throughput distributed caching, microservices backbones, network virtual appliances, software compilation pipelines, and web-tier infrastructure operating against external storage.

The instance delivers 96 GB of system memory, maintaining a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio characteristic of compute-focused platforms. Built on the Nitro hypervisor, it features a 150 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, though it includes no local NVMe storage or discrete GPUs. Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional parallel processing and memory throughput, highlighted by strong Geekbench multi-core scores, 64.06 GB/sec static web serving capacity, and over 76 million Redis SET operations per second. Conversely, single-thread performance and CPU-based LLM inference land in the median range. With high network bandwidth and robust multi-core density, the c7gn.12xlarge is designed for distributed microservices, network-intensive appliances, high-throughput caching tiers, and parallel build farms requiring high data throughput without local disk dependencies.
